record.paper_title: Some of my favorite open problems
record.context_brief: Finite potential energy for entire Ginzburg-Landau solutions
record.original_question: For any smooth solution u: R^2 → R^2 of the entire Ginzburg-Landau equation -Δu = u(1 - |u|^2) satisfying |u(x)| → 1 as |x| → ∞, must the potential-energy integral ∫_{R^2} (|u|^2 - 1)^2 be finite?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 2.5 ([BMR, Problem 2], [Br3, Open Problem 2]). Assume that u satisfies (2.5) and (2.6). Does (2.11) hold?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $u:\mathbb{R}^2\to\mathbb{R}^2$ be a smooth solution of the Ginzburg–Landau system
$$-\Delta u \;=\; u\bigl(1-|u|^2\bigr) \quad \text{on } \mathbb{R}^2,$$
and assume that
$$|u(x)| \longrightarrow 1 \quad \text{as } |x|\to\infty.$$
Must it then follow that the potential energy is finite, i.e.
$$\int_{\mathbb{R}^2}\bigl(|u(x)|^2-1\bigr)^2\,dx \;<\; \infty\,?$$
artifact.status_search_result: The question of whether every smooth entire solution of $-\Delta u=u(1-|u|^2)$ on $\mathbb{R}^2$ with $|u|\to 1$ at infinity automatically has finite potential integral $\int(|u|^2-1)^2$ is a well-known open problem repeatedly listed in Brezis's open-problem collections and in the Brezis–Mironescu–Rauch problem list. Searches did not reveal a resolution; the problem appears to remain open.
